angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 9,574,223 km at 123.61 pc = 1.04 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 17702: distance 123.609 pc, the paper's parallax inverted (Gaia DR1's where it revised the star's, else the Hipparcos reduction of van Leeuwen 2007; section 2.3; fractional uncertainty 0.052), at which the luminosity and radius hold (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433): 123.609 +/- 6.428 pc; Gaia DR3 gives this source no parallax (a two-parameter solution)
radiusSource: Radius 13.762 solar radii from McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 17702: radius 13.762 solar radii, implied by the fitted luminosity 843.922 solar luminosities (fractional uncertainty 0.91) and temperature (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433): 9,574,223 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. No mass is measured, so GM is 0, the records' unpublished value. Temperature 8392 +/- 4070 K from McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 17702: effective temperature 8392 +/- 4070 K, from the fit of a model atmosphere to the star's spectral energy distribution (goodness of fit Q 0.113) (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 17702: effective temperature 8392 +/- 4070 K, from the fit of a model atmosphere to the star's spectral energy distribution (goodness of fit Q 0.113) (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433)
spectralTypeSource: SIMBAD, * eta Tau: spectral type B7III
objectTypeSource: SIMBAD, * eta Tau: main object type Be*, Be Star
projectedRotationSpeedSource: SIMBAD, * eta Tau: projected rotation speed 145 km/s, the measurement SIMBAD prefers (2005yCat.3244....0G)

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, colored from the star's measured spectrum (Kharitonov, Tereshchenko & Knyazeva (1988), Spectrophotometric Catalogue of Stars (Alma-Ata), record 222) (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.

surfaceGravitySource: log g 4 from 2001A&A...378..861C; the 1 published value span log g 4 to 4, across which the limb law changes by at most 0.0% of the centre brightness (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2001A%26A...378..861C)
